Released 2026-10-04 · [downloads and checksums on GitHub](https://github.com/BuenGenio/backdown-releases/releases/tag/v1.0.0-beta.4) · [Download page](/download/)
The fourth beta of BackDown 1.0 and the first signed one: signed manifests of what your drives hold, a chain of custody for everything BackDown copies or deletes, updates for computers without a network, drive health from your other machines, and a new Duplicates view.

## Install

| Platform | Installer | Command line |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 | `backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.4_amd64.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu) or `.AppImage` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.4-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (static) |
| Linux ARM64 | `backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.4_arm64.deb` or `.AppImage` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.4-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (static) |
| macOS (Apple silicon + Intel) | `BackDown-1.0.0-beta.4.dmg` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.4-macos-universal.tar.gz` |
| Windows x86-64 | `BackDown-1.0.0-beta.4-x64.msi` (no administrator rights needed) | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.4-windows-x86_64.zip` |

**This release is signed.** `SHA256SUMS.txt.sig` is an Ed25519 signature of `SHA256SUMS.txt` by BackDown's release key, and `backdown update` checks it before installing anything; from this release on, an update without a valid signature is refused. To check by hand, see [Air-gapped computers](https://backdown.io/docs/guides/air-gapped/).

The installers and apps themselves still aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open the first time (for the command-line binary: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine backdown`). On Windows, SmartScreen may ask you to confirm once.

## What's new since beta.3

- **Signed manifests** (Forensic): `backdown manifest create` signs a statement of exactly what a drive held at a scan, every file's path, size and SHA-256 combined into one Merkle root, each chained to the drive's previous one. Anyone can check one with `backdown manifest verify`, or without BackDown from the algorithm in [the guide](https://backdown.io/docs/guides/manifests-and-attestations/).
- **Scheduled attestations** (Team): Settings > Attestations has the service sign a manifest of each drive after every scan, daily or weekly.
- **Chain of custody** (Forensic): every copy, move, deletion, link and merge BackDown makes goes into a hash-chained log, sealed with this installation's key. `backdown custody export` exports it, whole or for one job (other events are elided, the chain still verifies), `verify` checks a bundle anywhere, and `check` finds edits made to the index directly. The log is kept in every edition; it starts with this release.
- **Air-gapped computers** (Forensic): `backdown update --from FOLDER` installs a release carried over on a drive, its signature checked first and no network used. Checking such a folder (`--from … --check`) is free.
- **Drive health from your other machines** (Team): the machines you've added report their drives' health with each sync, shown in Activity and `backdown health --machines`, with a notification when one gets worse.
- **Duplicates, reworked**: one entry per set of identical files that opens to its copies, or grouped by the folders they're in, with the filter bar applied, thumbnails, and ticks that hand copies to Free up.
- **Safer git history**: the browser's git view no longer lets a repository found on a drive fetch from the network or run programs its own configuration names.

## Known limitations

- Built locally, not by CI. Every test passed on Linux; the macOS and Windows builds are checked but haven't yet run on those systems. Please report anything that doesn't work: https://github.com/BuenGenio/backdown-releases/issues
- The installers aren't signed or notarised by Apple or Microsoft.
- Pro, Team and Forensic features are free during the beta; pricing may change before 1.0.

Documentation: https://backdown.io/docs/. Provided as-is, without warranty, for evaluation.
